A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SuperMentor study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original error-prediction experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1K, including architecture comparisons, perturbation studies, transfer evaluations and loss ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, medical-image evaluation, unseen-domain tests, joint-source training and EigenCAM case studies.

M1.justification: The backbone, two independent MLP streams, distillation-plus-binary-classification objective and frozen mentee remain unchanged. SuperMentor still uses ViT and PIFGSM training images with epsilon 1/255. Explicit loss formulas clarify existing components; joint-source training is an additional experimental control.

E1.justification: Appendices H–I add colorectal histology classification using NCTCRCHE100K and five unseen ImageNet-related domains: three ImageNet9 background-recombination conditions, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch. These substantially extend the original natural-image and synthetic-corruption coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's comparisons among mentor variants, v2 evaluates SER, MCP, CPE, DTC, ConfidNet, TrustScore and Steep Slope Loss. Their participation is documented in Table 1 and Tables S2–S3 and S5, substantially expanding external comparison methods.

E3.justification: Original dataset splits, balanced accuracy, preprocessing and 40-epoch/batch-512 settings are retained. Added experiments specify three-value threshold grids for MCP, CPE and DTC, a CIFAR-10 control mixing ID, SpN and PIFGSM training data, and evaluation without training on the additional OOD domains.

E4.justification: v2 adds joint-source training to test whether ID/OOD data supplement adversarial training, robustness evaluations on unseen background and depiction shifts, and EigenCAM case studies comparing mentor/mentee attention. The original loss ablation, perturbation analysis and t-SNE visualization remain, despite relocation.

E5.justification: Retained experiments preserve their three-run means and standard deviations, including the appendix ablation and transfer tables. No changed run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are introduced; new comparisons mainly provide point estimates.

E6.justification: New results include ImageNet baseline comparisons, 79.1% for joint-source training versus 78.0% for AA-only training, medical-task scores and unseen-domain accuracies of 58.68–69.24%. These are added comparisons/settings rather than demonstrated version-to-version performance gains. Table S5 reports a medical average of 81.9%, although its nine displayed SuperMentor scores average approximately 79.6%.

T1.justification: The correctness definition and underlying objectives remain unchanged. v2 writes out standard KL-distillation and binary-cross-entropy formulas for previously named losses and explains baseline scoring rules, without introducing substantive theoretical results, proofs or new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The four central contributions remain. The abstract replaces the 78% headline with an ImageNet baseline-comparison claim, while the conclusion adds claims about medical applicability, unseen-domain robustness and the mentor's diagnostic capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 interprets joint-training gains as evidence of overlapping error patterns and recommends AA-only training on computational grounds. It also argues that training-data source matters more than baseline losses and strategies, and uses EigenCAM examples to claim diagnostic capabilities and non-overlapping mentor/mentee vulnerabilities. These substantially extend v1's interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit loss formulas, baseline decision rules and threshold values, and the target transformer layer used for EigenCAM. Existing optimizer, hardware, preprocessing and training-budget disclosures remain unchanged, as does the promise to release code, models and data.

R1.justification: Related work now addresses directly relevant failure/trustworthiness predictors, including ConfidNet, TrustScore and SSL, and distinguishes the approach from selective prediction, rejection learning and learning to defer. This substantially develops the novelty positioning beyond v1's emphasis on OOD detection and adversarial training.

P1.justification: Much existing prose and the main section sequence remain closely matched. v2 adds a baseline/metric subsection and Impact Statement, expands the discussion, and reorganizes appendices while relocating split details, loss-ablation discussion and visualization material. These are localized revisions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 switches the main text to two columns, adds baseline tables and an EigenCAM figure, and redraws Figures 4–5 with different proportions and legends. Split, ablation and t-SNE displays move into appendices; the redundant CIFAR summary Figure 6 disappears while its underlying results remain available.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's internal mentor comparisons and synthetic corruptions, v2's published-method comparisons and additional domain tests make usefulness and generalization easier to assess. However, the new medical headline has an inconsistent average (Table S5), and the categorical claim of non-overlapping vulnerabilities rests on two EigenCAM examples (Appendix J). These reporting and interpretation problems limit confidence in the expanded reliability claims, leaving a modest net quality improvement.
